title: Sudowrite Pricing 2026: Which Plan Should You Get?
summary: Sudowrite pricing ranges from $19 to $59 monthly, or $10 to $44 monthly if you pay annually. See the breakdown for each plan's costs and limits.
body_markdown:
## Which Sudowrite Plan Fits Three Everyday Writing Uses


Buy the cheapest plan that covers your heaviest month: Hobby & Student for a hobbyist, Professional for a novelist redrafting, and Professional or Max for a ghostwriter or small team.


The deciding figure is cost per credit at annual billing, shown below per 100,000 credits for each plan.


About $4.44 for Hobby & Student and $2.20 for Professional, against $2.20 for Max, which means at the same usage level, Max costs far less.


Upgrade from Hobby & Student to Professional and the unit price roughly halves. Upgrade again to Max and **the unit price halves** .


Moving to Max is therefore a decision about both capacity and savings. It pays only when your heaviest months would otherwise need top-ups costing more than the gap between the two plans.


Check that top-up price on Sudowrite's own pricing page before you decide.


### Hobbyist finishing a short novel


When you are drafting a few chapters, mostly first pass, credits are spent slowly, because little text is regenerated. Hobby & Student, at 225,000 credits for $10, is enough if your busiest month fits inside that balance.


If you overrun only now and then, that doesn't justify Professional. Compare the top-up price against the plan gap, and pay the smaller of the two.


### Novelist redrafting a full manuscript


Because redrafting spends the same passages again on every pass, credit use tracks the number of passes, not the length of the book. **Professional holds 1,000,000 credits** per month at $22 on annual billing.


If a redrafting month overruns Hobby & Student, it would be bought at the higher rate, so Professional is the plan that fits. Max pays only if your heaviest month exceeds 450,000.


### Ghostwriter or two-person team


With several manuscripts running at once, the heaviest month is the one to budget against. The editor's analysis shows Max gives 2,000,000 credits at $2.20 per 100,000, well below Professional's rate, so you gain per credit by choosing it.


Start on Professional, and move up only after a month where top-ups cost more than the upgrade would have. Confirm on the pricing page whether two people can work from one plan before you buy a second.
